title: Making 'April in Paris' with Bill Davis and Bill Jennings
summary: Thomas suggests the tune, fixes bass recording, and the 'one more time' ending later made famous by Basie.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So I had... Bill was recording on Epic Records. And the guy that was doing the recording was out of town. So I got an idea... One thing, I always thought about ideas. I thought about recording Bill. But the A&R man was out of town, the one that had the charts over at Columbia. So I called Bill and I said, 'Man, make an arrangement on 'April In Paris.'" Because "April In Paris" was a song coming out, it's a vocal, and it was getting kind of big. It was an old tune anyhow. I said, "Make an arrangement on 'April In Paris'." I just thought that would be something to give him.

So we did the recording at Nola Studio. And I had had this hassle with him about that bass. I knew he wasn't getting enough bass on those recordings. So I found out that the bass was coming out at the bottom, and the treble was coming out up there further. I got ahold of the A&R man, who was a German; he'd just come to the... And he did... Everywhere I told him to put a mike, he put it. So I told him to put that mike down there and catch the bass... And Bill Jennings made the arrangement. So we recorded it. And to this day, I don't know who suggested "one more time." Because when we got to the ending... It was the ending, so we could repeat this. And somebody, either Chris or somebody suggested "one more time," then we put that "one more time" in there, went back to that [SINGS REFRAIN]...

And Bill later on made the arrangement for Basie. And I worked out a deal for Bill to be on the recording date. He was down in Atlantic City. I had to go through all kinds of jazz, because, see, Bill is one record label and Basie is on another. So I had to get a marriage between the record companies. And I got that deal going... And Bill eventually missed the date, but Basie made the record anyway. And Basie kind of outshone Bill.

It's a funny thing how that expression got so popular, 'one more time.' And Bill Jennings made the arrangement, which made the arrangement so beautiful. Because he played the melody of 'April In Paris,' the little whine(?) thing going on, but he didn't do a whole lot of ad-libbing on it. Because there's nothing in the world greater than the melody. If a melody is good, you can play it. And that left... Even some of these popular songs, the melodies just live forever. That's still going on. And it really comes from the old masters writing them simple things. 'April In Paris'... [SINGS REFRAIN]
